features.name: South Polar Nitrogen Cap
features.description: Triton's south polar cap is a bright sheet of frozen nitrogen and methane seen by Voyager 2 during southern summer. Seasonal sunlight can warm the frost just enough to mobilize nitrogen, feeding Triton's thin atmosphere and helping drive the geyser-like plumes that made this moon famous.

details.label: Temperature
details.value: Voyager 2 measured about -235 C near Triton

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Bright southern cap and streaked polar terrain on the Voyager hemisphere

details.label: Source note
details.value: NASA describes Triton as one of the coldest objects Voyager visited, with nitrogen frost covering much of the surface.

features.name: Hili Plume Field
features.description: Voyager 2 saw dark plume deposits crossing Triton's southern polar terrain, evidence that sunlight can trigger nitrogen geysers through translucent frost. The plumes were only a few active jets in a much broader seasonal system, but they proved Triton was not a dead iceball at the edge of the Solar System.

details.label: Science value
details.value: One of the clearest signs of present-day geologic activity on Triton

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark wind-blown streaks over the southern cap

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Representative plume-field anchor placed on the visible southern streak terrain

features.name: Mahilani Plume Field
features.description: Mahilani marks the second classic plume region associated with Voyager's Triton encounter. Its dark fallout streaks are thought to be carried by Triton's tenuous winds, turning small jets into long surface signatures that reveal both active geology and atmospheric motion.

details.label: Process
details.value: Solar heating through nitrogen frost can pressurize gas below the surface

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dark linear deposits in southern polar terrain

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Representative anchor on the Voyager-mapped plume-streak zone

features.name: Tuonela Planitia
features.description: Tuonela Planitia is an elongated northern plain interpreted as a cryolava lake or resurfaced basin. It cuts across Triton's strange cantaloupe terrain, giving the map a strong contrast between cellular older-looking texture and smoother icy plains that may have flowed or ponded.

details.label: Approximate size
details.value: About 400 by 150 km in published descriptions

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern smooth/walled plain set among pitted cantaloupe terrain

features.name: Ruach Planitia
features.description: Ruach Planitia is one of Triton's prominent smooth plains, a place where icy material appears to have resurfaced older terrain. Plains like Ruach make Triton look geologically young: impact craters are scarce, and the surface has been repeatedly modified by icy volcanism, collapse, and frost transport.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Smooth northern plain near Tuonela Planitia and the cantaloupe terrain

details.label: Interpretation
details.value: A possible cryovolcanic or volatile-rich resurfacing province

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Educational anchor aligned to the visible northern plains cluster

features.name: Set Catena
features.description: Set Catena is a chain of regularly spaced pits cutting through Triton's northern terrain. Pit chains can form when the crust collapses over voids or fractures, so this feature is a useful stop for reading how Triton's icy shell stretched, broke, and possibly vented volatile-rich material.

details.label: Control coordinate
details.value: About 22 N, 33.5 E

details.label: Typical pit spacing
details.value: Published summaries describe spacing near 20 km

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Linear pit chain in the mapped northern hemisphere

features.name: Bubembe Regio
features.description: Bubembe Regio is part of Triton's named northern terrain province. Its cellular, dimpled texture belongs to the famous 'cantaloupe terrain' seen nowhere else in the Solar System, probably shaped by icy diapirs, collapse, or repeated deformation of a nitrogen-rich crust.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Regio: a broad named region with distinct appearance

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Dimpled northern province west of the main mapped plains cluster

features.name: Monad Regio
features.description: Monad Regio contains some of the most recognizable cantaloupe terrain on Triton. Rounded cells and pitted boundaries make the crust look kneaded rather than cratered, hinting that Triton's interior and volatile cycle have repeatedly renewed its icy surface.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern dimpled terrain surrounding Tuonela and Ruach Planitiae

details.label: Science value
details.value: A key terrain for testing how icy shells deform on captured Kuiper Belt objects

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Representative regional anchor on the Voyager global map

features.name: Cipango Planum
features.description: Cipango Planum is a broad, relatively smooth plain in the mapped hemisphere. It helps connect the story of Triton's surface: some areas are heavily textured and cellular, while nearby plains look resurfaced by soft, volatile-rich ice that behaved more like lava than rock.

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Low northern to equatorial smooth terrain near the Set Catena area

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Representative plain anchor placed within the mapped Cipango province

features.name: Leviathan Patera
features.description: Leviathan Patera is one of Triton's named volcanic-looking depressions. Features like this are not basaltic volcanoes; on Triton, eruptions and collapses would involve nitrogen, water ice, ammonia-bearing slurries, or other cryogenic materials in a world colder than any active volcanic body on Earth.

details.label: Feature type
details.value: Patera: an irregular crater or volcanic depression

details.label: Map cue
details.value: Northern mapped terrain near pit chains and smooth plains

details.label: Coordinate note
details.value: Representative anchor for the named cryovolcanic province

features.name: North Polar Seasonal Region
features.description: Triton's north pole was poorly lit for Voyager 2, but it matters because Triton's extreme axial geometry lets each pole take long turns facing the Sun. That seasonal forcing moves nitrogen frost between hemispheres and may change the atmosphere over decades.

details.label: Seasonal context
details.value: Both poles take turns facing the Sun because of Triton's unusual orbit and orientation

details.label: Map cue
details.value: High-latitude reference point, not a sharply imaged named feature

features.name: Retrograde Captured Orbit
features.description: Triton is the only large moon in the Solar System with a retrograde orbit: it travels around Neptune opposite the planet's rotation. That dynamical oddity is the strongest clue that Triton began as a Kuiper Belt object and was captured by Neptune rather than forming in place.

details.label: Real orbit
details.value: About 354,800 km from Neptune's center

details.label: Inclination
details.value: About 157 degrees to Neptune's equator, making the orbit retrograde

details.label: Scene note
details.value: Shown as a tilted outer companion path around Neptune
